output.brief: Pellacott's 2026 VA-220 valves are failing, and the leak-test certificates behind its score don't reflect real testing. The lab teardown found seat leakage with a deformed seal in 38 of 41 returned valves. Unused 2026 Pellacott valves leaked at the seat in 11% of a helium retest (44 of 400). Durrant-Hale valves showed none, and 2025 Pellacott valves almost none. When claims are matched to serial numbers, the failure rate is the same for new and legacy installers and for firmware 4.1 and 4.2, so installers and firmware are not the cause. The calibration contractor found Pellacott's only VA-220 leak rig out of service since 9 January 2026. Its last test was in December 2025. The 2026 certificates repeat four fixed sequences of values that also appear in November 2025 certificates. The score rose because complete-looking records earned credit, not because quality improved. Do not release the six held lots on fresh certificates. Quarantine all 2026-built Pellacott stock, suspend dock-to-stock, and release only after Brenmoor's own helium testing. Drop the installer remediation plan and chargebacks. Secure alternative supply, mainly Durrant-Hale, to avoid the line stoppage. The seal change and the line change cannot yet be separated, so reverting to Ferrand is premature. Whether other suppliers' records are also unreliable is unknown. Audit them promptly.
